chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman performing Tamattu': When she enters the state of Ihram while pure, then menstruates before she completes her Tamattu', she performs Sa'i and does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure. Then she completes her Tawaf, and her Tamattu' is complete. And if she entered Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'i and does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَتْ: She entered the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُتَمَتِّعَةِ: The woman performing Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.سَعَتْ: She performed Sa'i (the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.طَافَتْ: She performed Tawaf (the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a woman performing Tamattu' Hajj if she menstruates before completing her rituals?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* by distinguishing between a woman who enters Ihram in a state of purity versus one already menstruating, establishing that menstruation suspends the performance of rituals rather than invalidating the Hajj itself. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of the Hajj is not contingent upon the immediate completion of all rites in a single sequence, but rather on the eventual fulfillment of Sa'i and Tawaf after the state of *hadath* (minor impurity) is removed. The narration underscores the practical ease (*rukhas*) granted to women, ensuring their Hajj remains complete even if the order of rituals is adjusted due to natural biological cycles.
